My boyfriend does not believe fat shaming works. Anyone have any evidence to help me change his mind?
Honestly, I don't know/don't care if it does. Fatpeoplehate has always been a place that exists for the purpose of venting anger and frustration, not to shame people into losing weight.

I'll tell you what didn't help me when I was a total fatty a few years ago: people saying I looked fine. That I didn't need to lose weight; I was pretty, funny, smart, etc. I had to realize how big I had gotten when I had to put on a size 17 pants. Even that day, my friends were saying, "Well, maybe the sizes just run small, you look great!"

Now that my BMI has been in a healthy range for a while, I'm trying to get back in shape. Yes, I'm thin, but after knee surgery, I am weak. I used FPH as motivation to not go back to what I was once becoming. Plus, sometimes, there were some informative links about the obesity epidemic, how obesity affects mental health, etc.

I found FPH through a sub for abuse survivors. A post was made, asking how members of that sub can also be members of FPH. People were talking of banning others simply for being associated with FPH, from what I remember.

Then, there's an article JFK wrote on the problem in 1960. (http://www.ihpra.org/soft_american.htm) I haven't looked into formatting on here, but there is a link for you. Basically, he was concerned that Americans would become complacent with being overweight, then obese, and would eventually be unable to defend ourselves. I read that YEARS ago, and the whole FA movement just disgusts me because it is weakening everyone physically and emotionally. Even when I worked as a personal trainer, I would never tell someone they are fine the way they are. I didn't like excuses. Any time a client would say, "This is too hard for me!" I'd respond with, "If it's too hard, you're too weak, and your body needs this."

And you know what? They were all losing weight. Some of those clients, I still talk to, years later. And they say to me, "You know, IggyReilly, I still hear your voice in my head when I work out, telling me to stop making excuses." Sometimes I had to get mean, to send a clear message to them. They didn't like it at first, but it got them results. I'd give them shit if they told me they had a "cheat day" 1 or 2 weeks into their lifestyle changes, when the form on those last reps was slipping, and when they'd try to fatlogic their way out of their goals.

So, in my experience, coddling people into being healthy doesn't work. Similar to drug addiction, sometimes you've gotta just give extra tough love to the addicts. If they don't change, it's their loss, and they don't deserve any respect after they've been shown what they're doing to themselves and loved ones.
Thanks for taking the time to type that reply and I totally couldn't agree more.
